Standard: The durability of propeller system hardware is such that the propeller system capability established in 7.5.1 standards is not adversely affected, propeller system operating limits are not exceeded, and detrimental permanent deformation or damage does not occur when the propeller system is operated, under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.5.2 for the stated life documented in technical data. Durability includes resistance to fatigue, cracking, delamination, creep, permanent set, engine and propeller fluids, ultraviolet radiation, wear, and tolerance to environments defined in 7.5.2. Part-specific critical material, processing, and manufacturing characteristics, and associated controls, are established for PCPs IAW 14 CFR 35.16. Operating limitations and life management actions required to maintain propeller system structural integrity and functionality (e.g., component inspection, repair, and replacement requirements) are based on 7.5.2 and are recorded in the technical data. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of PCP product definition data (e.g., models, drawings) verifies that part-specific critical material, processing, and manufacturing characteristics, and associated controls, are defined.
(2) Examination of the service management plan, and applicable maintenance manuals (e.g., TOs, Naval Aviation Technical Information Products) verifies that PCPs, and associated life management actions, are defined and documented. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis is conducted to determine minimum fatigue life and mandatory replacement times, and to define mature and repeatable material, processing, and manufacturing control parameters required to achieve that life for each PCP. Scatter factors used to establish life limits are substantiated.
  (2) Analysis shows all critical vibratory frequencies, mode shapes, and stresses as a function of blade angle and rpm. Analysis is calibrated to test results. Campbell diagrams are prepared to verify margin to potential resonances, particularly at sustained operating ranges. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Propeller components including the blades and barrel, pitch changing mechanism, pitch lock, negative torque signal, control unit, and ice control system are durability tested to establish their capability to perform their function for the operational life defined in technical data. Testing includes fatigue evaluation under combined steady and vibratory loads as needed to determine failure locations, failure modes, vibratory capability, and life limits. A complete teardown inspection is conducted at the conclusion of the test. Records are made of failures, wear, distortion, and other unusual conditions.
    (2) Lab test: Whirl stand testing, including vibratory stress surveys and endurance tests, of the propeller system are conducted to verify durability. A complete teardown inspection is conducted at the conclusion of the test. Records are made of failures, wear, distortion, and other unusual conditions.
    (3) Lab test: The following propeller-and-engine combination tests are conducted on a sea-level test stand. An instrumented vibratory stress survey is conducted to determine stress characteristics of the propeller and engine combination. Endurance tests are conducted IAW JSSG-2009, Propeller Subsystem, Propeller and Engine Test Stand Tests, 50-Hour Test, Cyclic Tests paragraph or per the conditions and success criteria as specified in 14 CFR 35.39. Post-test teardown inspection of hardware is accomplished to document condition. Minimum endurance test duration is 50 hours.
    (4) Ground test: Installed ground testing of the integrated propeller system/engine/air vehicle is conducted on the air vehicle being certified. Instrumented ground vibratory stress surveys are conducted on the propeller at each air vehicle nacelle. Static crosswind conditions are included in the evaluation. Documented propeller operating limitations are confirmed. Inspection of all test articles before, during, and after test verifies no unexpected interactions, failures, or wear. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (5) Lab test: Endurance testing of the propeller-and-engine combination is conducted IAW JSSG-2009, Propeller Subsystem, Propeller and Engine Test Stand Tests, 150-Hour Test paragraph or per the conditions and success criteria as specified in 14 CFR 35.39. Post-test teardown inspection of hardware is accomplished to document condition. Minimum endurance test duration is 150 hours.
    (6) Flight test: Installed flight testing of the integrated propeller system/engine/air vehicle is conducted on the air vehicle being certified. Instrumented flight vibratory stress surveys are conducted on the propeller at each air vehicle nacelle. Crosswind and maneuver conditions are included in the evaluation. Documented propeller operating limitations are confirmed. Inspection of all test articles before, during, and after test verifies no unexpected interactions, failures or wear.
